subject: general
question: Which of the following statements about lysosomes is correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the **Golgi apparatus**. They are often referred to as the "**suicidal bags**" of the cell.
 
• These organelles contain a wide variety of **hydrolytic enzymes** (**hydrolases**), such as **lipases**, **proteases**, and **carbohydrases**, which are optimally active at an **acidic pH**. These enzymes are responsible for digesting **carbohydrates**, **proteins**, **lipids**, and **nucleic acids**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The synthesis of **fats** (**lipids**) and **steroids** primarily takes place in the **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum** (**SER**), not in the lysosomes. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Protein synthesis** is the primary function of **ribosomes**, which may be found floating freely in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum** (**RER**). Lysosomes do not synthesize proteins; they degrade them. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Growth hormones** are signaling molecules produced by specialized **endocrine glands**, such as the **pituitary gland**. They are not contained or produced within lysosomes. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structure and Discovery:** 
 
 
• **Lysosomes** were discovered by the Belgian cytologist **Christian de Duve** in **1955**.
 
• They are typically **spherical** in shape and are enclosed by a **single unit membrane** to prevent the powerful enzymes from leaking and destroying the rest of the cell.
 
 
 
• **Mechanism of Action:** 
 
 
• Lysosomes maintain an internal **acidic environment** (around **pH 4.5 to 5.0**) through **proton pumps** in their membranes that transport **H+ ions** from the cytosol.
 
• They are involved in **autophagy** (digesting the cell's own damaged organelles) and **heterophagy** (digesting external materials like bacteria or food particles taken in via **endocytosis**).
 
 
 
• **Types of Lysosomes:** 
 
 
• **Primary Lysosomes:** Newly formed vesicles from the **Golgi body** containing inactive enzymes.
 
• **Secondary Lysosomes:** Formed by the fusion of a primary lysosome with a **phagosome** or **food vacuole**; this is where active digestion occurs.
 
• **Residual Bodies:** Lysosomes containing undigested material that are eventually eliminated via **exocytosis**.
 
 
 
• **Clinical Significance:** 
 
 
• Malfunctioning of lysosomal enzymes can lead to **Lysosomal Storage Diseases** (**LSDs**), such as **Tay-Sachs disease** or **Gaucher's disease**, where undigested substances accumulate and damage tissues.
 
• They are highly abundant in **animal cells**, particularly in **White Blood Cells** (**leukocytes**) like **macrophages**, which utilize lysosomal enzymes to destroy pathogens.
